messages:
anjali: Quick sync — I sketched a 'model life runway' plan we need to finalize before next quarter. High level: three migration lanes (fast, staged 90d, legacy 6mo), per-lane acceptance sets, and a small compatibility shim for older SDKs. Looking for engineering constraints + comm plan.
ben: +1 on lanes. curious about who owns acceptance sets — product or research?
mike: research owns core evals but product should own customer-facing acceptance criteria. we can produce model-level perf + hallucination checks.
tara: what sample sizes are we expecting for benchmark gates? small n leads to noisy decisions.
mike: i'd standardize: smoke (n=500), canary gate (n=2k), full acceptance (n=10k) for token-level metrics. seq distribution should match real traffic.
anjali: nice, keep the three gates. also propose a soft-pin vs hard-pin semantics: soft-pin = recommended default, auto-fallback allowed; hard-pin = exact model id locked for tenant. sales/legal need wording.
linda: from customer success — customers want explicit migration windows and a one-click rollback. can we promise a 72h rollback window for dedicated tenants?
ben: engineering note: 72h rollback requires retention of previous model binaries and KV cache fallback paths. storage + cost impact is moderate.
mike: ops: we'll need a 'compat shim' to translate older prompts/params for some family of models (small adapter layer). low-lift for NLP-only models, heavier for multimodal.
anjali: proposal: for legacy lane require shim + acceptance set. staged lane allows optional shim. fast lane = no shim — customer must be ready.
tara: flags/rollouts: suggest canary % by tenant cohort: 1%, 5%, 20%, 100% with metric gating at each step. also include manual hold for customer-initiated pause.
linda: comms: plan to send migration notice 30d before staged, 90d for legacy. include sample prompts and a quick self-serve test harness.
ben: portability checklist: model artifact compatibility, quantization profile, tokenizer sanity, deterministic seed test. share the checklist in repo.
mike: benchmark command I'm using for reproducibility:
```
./bench --model modelX:v2 --queries queries.json --runs 5000 --seq 512 --capture=latency,perplexity
```
we should check latency p95 + rouge/emd for quality depending on task.
anjali: decision items: 1) gate sample sizes (agree on mike's numbers?) 2) soft vs hard pin policy text 3) rollback SLA 4) comm windows 5) shim scope.
ben: i'm okay with mike's numbers. on soft/hard pin text i can draft a one-paragraph policy for legal to review.
tara: i'll add rollout gating + metrics thresholds to the rollout playbook. propose p95 latency delta <20% and failure/error rate change <0.1pp as automatic gates.
linda: CS will prepare customer communication templates and the self-serve harness link.
catalog-bot: New model entry created: modelX:v3 (provisional). Metadata: family=falconx, size=13B.
mike: one more engineering constraint — for 6mo legacy lane we must keep quantized fp16 artifacts for ~180 days to ensure rollback. storage estimate: ~120GB per model across shards.
anjali: thanks — next steps: ben drafts pin policy + legal blurb, tara updates rollout playbook with thresholds, mike finalizes benchmark harness and uploads commands, linda drafts comms + test harness. I'll compile into a short launch checklist by EOD Friday.
ben: ack.
tara: ack.
mike: ack.
linda: ack.
anjali: tagging @sales for visibility — we may need to offer migration credits for large customers who opt into fast lane.
ben: note: add opt-out path in tenant settings and API for programmatic pin.
mike: putting a TODO in the repo for the shim adapter spec.
anjali: great — if there are no objections i'll create a short RFC doc and a single-entry ticket per lane this afternoon.
ben: go for it :thumbsup:
